title: Washington Pivots Military Funds to Latin America, Slashing European and Middle East Aid
snippet: The U.S. is redirecting tens of millions of dollars in security assistance away from traditional strategic allies to reinforce ideologically aligned governments across the Western Hemisphere.
content:
WASHINGTON — In a major shift of foreign policy priorities, the United States is stripping millions of dollars in foreign military assistance from long-standing partners in Europe and the Middle East to bolster funding for ideological allies in the Americas.

Strategic Realignment in the Americas

The reallocation reflects a broader pivot by the administration toward prioritizing border enforcement, counter-narcotics efforts, and regional alignments in the Western Hemisphere. Under the new directive, funding originally earmarked for security enhancement programs in Central and Eastern Europe, as well as several Middle Eastern defense partners, will be diverted to key governments in Central and South America.

Foreign policy analysts and lawmakers on Capitol Hill have voiced contrasting views on the strategy. While proponents argue that securing the immediate neighborhood is vital for national security and curbing illegal migration, critics warn that reducing support for European and Middle Eastern security could weaken traditional alliances and create strategic vacuums in key geopolitical hotspots.
